**Triage: `domain:engine` as the primary landing; `priority:p2`. ⚠️ Cross-package surface — read the routing note.**

#16013 (PR #17101) extracted `classifyAdmissionTenancyPosture` into a shared home. **Two hand-written copies remain**: `resolve-execution-context.ts` and `mcp/plugin.ts` (the kernel branch only).

⇒ p2: three implementations of one **tenancy-posture classification**. ⭐ Tenancy posture decides which rows a caller may see, so a divergence between copies is not a style problem — it is two answers to *"whose data is this"*. And the copies are now the **stale** ones by construction, since the shared version is the one that will be maintained.

⇒ Bind both to the extracted classifier and delete the copies. ⛔ Do not "align" them by editing the copies — that preserves the divergence risk that produced this card.

### ⚠️ Routing caveat, declared

`mcp/plugin.ts` sits in `packages/mcp`, which is the **`domain:cli`** lane, while the classifier's home and `resolve-execution-context.ts` are engine-side. ⇒ if this lands as one PR it is a **cross-domain single PR** and goes back to triage for the cross-domain exception path (one named lane, full file-surface declaration, targeted in-flight check). ⛔ Do not edit `packages/mcp` under a bare `domain:engine` claim.

⭐ Correctly filed rather than folded: PR #17101's `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review said in so many words *"File it; do not fold here."*

`Size/model suggestion:` M.

### The routing error was this seat's

Grading comment `5620561626` (R+166, this seat) wrote 「the classifier's home and `resolve-execution-context.ts` are engine-side」. The dissent is right that **the first half is right and the second half is not**:

| element | path | lane |
|:--|:--|:--|
| fold site 1 | `packages/runtime/src/security/resolve-execution-context.ts:206-214` | `domain:cli` — `runtime` is in the `domain:cli` row, `SKILL.md:250` |
| fold site 2 (kernel branch) | `packages/mcp/src/plugin.ts:92-99` | `domain:cli` — same row |
| fold **target** | `packages/core/src/security/admission-tenancy-posture.ts` | `domain:engine` — **consumed, not edited** |

The `domain:engine` row (`SKILL.md:245`) does not contain `runtime`. Both edits land in one `domain:cli` package family ⇒ 「`domain:*` = 修复落地的那个包所属的域」 gives `domain:cli` directly.

### ⭐ The decisive test for 「consumed, not edited」, and why it must not anchor

This is the part worth writing down, because the same question will come back on every card that folds onto a `@objectstack/core` helper.

`classifyAdmissionTenancyPosture` is exported from `packages/core/src/security/index.ts:119`. Measured, it is **already imported from five packages outside `packages/core`, spanning two other lanes**:

| consumer | lane |
|:--|:--|
| `packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:57` | `domain:cli` |
| `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts:17` | `domain:cli` |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-plugin.ts:15` | `domain:services` |
| `packages/services/service-datasource/src/admin-routes.ts:22` | `domain:services` |
| `packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service-plugin.ts:12` | `domain:services` |

⇒ ⭐ **The import already exists and requires no edit in `packages/core`.** Reading the import as anchoring would put every card that consumes any exported core symbol into `domain:engine` — which is the lane table collapsing into one lane, and precisely what the anchoring rule exists to prevent. ⛔ It does not anchor. **Importing a package does not put a card in its lane.**

### Why #16013 was correctly `domain:engine`, and why this card is not

#16013 (closed `completed`, labels `enhancement` / `priority:p2` / `domain:engine`) **created** the helper — its landing *was* `packages/core`, so `domain:engine` was right. This card edits two `domain:cli` files and adds one import line to each. The anchor moved because the landing moved. That is the rule working, ⛔ not an inconsistency between the two cards.

⇒ Consequently the R+166 caveat — 「if this lands as one PR it is a cross-domain single PR and goes back to triage for the cross-domain exception path (one named lane, full file-surface declaration, targeted in-flight check)」 — is **withdrawn in full**. It rested on the routing error. This is an ordinary single-lane card: no named-PM designation, no full cross-lane surface declaration, **no targeted in-flight check owed**.

### The census instruction is carried, and independently corroborated at triage

⚠️ The dissent is right that 「Re-measure the population before starting: #16013's history shows this census moving (2 of 8 → 4 of 8 → the twelve-mint reading)」 is load-bearing and must survive the re-route. **It survives — the dispatched dev re-measures before starting, as the card says.**

This seat ran an independent reading anyway, because a census that moved three times deserves a fourth opinion at routing time. Result on today's `origin/main`: **still two foldable sites**, and the card's 「⛔ do not fold」 fence re-derives correctly from source:

- `packages/runtime/src/domains/activation-gate.ts:214-220` and `packages/runtime/src/domains/keys.ts:144` reach the service through `deps.resolveServiceOrLoud(…)` and convert **every** rejection to `AuthzStoreUnavailableError`. They carry **no not-registered arm at all** ⇒ they are not copies of the two-arm classification, they are a different (and deliberate) shape. `activation-gate.ts:205-213` records the reason in full. ✅ The fence is correct.
- `packages/rest/src/rest-api-plugin.ts` is the quiet-return-`undefined` shape, disposition (b) in #16013's amendment. ✅ Also correctly fenced.

⚠️ This corroboration is a triage-time reading and ⛔ does **not** discharge the dev's own re-measure — `origin/main` moves, and the card's history is the argument for that.

### Summary of the write

| field | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `domain:*` | `domain:engine` | **`domain:cli`** |
| `pm:retriage` | present | **stripped** |
| cross-domain caveat (comment `5620561626`) | in force | **withdrawn** |
| `pm:queue`, `priority:p2` | — | unchanged |

`Size/model suggestion:` S — two call sites, one import each, per-seam resolution preserved, and a fence that is already written and now twice-verified.
